findings.title: Acceptance does not bind predecessor acceptance/output versions to the successor Run
reproduction: Create active Goal, current Decision D1, predecessor A with D1 input, and successor B with dependency_task_ids=[A].
Claim/report/independently accept A through normal HTTP; claim/report B while A is accepted.
Use normal W04 Decision D2 supersession and independently accepted ChangeProposal apply to replace D1. A becomes NEEDS_REVALIDATION; B remains EXECUTION_REPORTED.
POST acceptance for B: server returns 201 with PASS and commits B ACCEPTED.

Second independent test: before accepting B, REVALIDATE A, build fresh ContextBundle, SUBMIT, execute and accept a replacement A Run with a new Artifact and new AcceptanceReceipt. B original Run still returns 201/PASS and becomes ACCEPTED.
findings.expected: Reject B old execution when a mandatory dependency loses validity or its bound acceptance/output version changes; revalidation/new execution must use current dependency bindings.
findings.cause: Claim checks current dependenciesReady but does not freeze predecessor AcceptanceReceipt/output version vector into the Run. ContextBundle records dependency status text only. acceptanceSnapshot neither evaluates dependency readiness nor compares dependency versions, so both preparation and final recheck omit this state.
findings.impact: A successor can be accepted from obsolete prerequisites even though all its own frozen JSON checks pass. Checking current ACCEPTED status alone would not close the reproduced replacement/ABA case.
findings.fix_boundary: Bind exact dependency acceptance/output versions at admission and revalidate them on report/acceptance/final commit. Preserve immutable historical receipts; do not rewrite W04 accepted history.

findings.title: Identical output bytes have no current-Run deduplicated provenance path

contract_basis.text: Artifact UNIQUE(project_id,content_hash,kind); byte-content deduplication; preserve multiple origins by references without replacing provenance.

reproduction: Create two ordinary tasks and distinct executor Runs in one project.

Second Run independently uploads the identical bytes and attempts its own REPORT seal: HTTP 409 STATE_CONFLICT, one Artifact remains. This duplicate-identity rejection itself matches the frozen unique constraint.

Provide trusted current-Run observation of those identical output bytes and report the existing deduplicated Artifact ID from the second Run: HTTP 422 GATE_FAILED because Artifact.run_id/produced_by belong to the first Run.
findings.expected: Keep the specified content uniqueness while retaining authenticated per-Run production references so repeated identical results can be reported and independently accepted.
findings.impact: Routine stable/repeated JSON results cannot complete through either creation or reuse in the current normal runtime lifecycle. This is an integration gap between existing dedup semantics and Run provenance checks, not a claim that duplicate Artifact identities must be allowed.
findings.fix_boundary: Do not delete or relax the frozen unique index. Add a contract-consistent deduplicated content/reference lineage path with current-Run observation/provenance binding, including acceptance validation.
